one_month_reasoning: The one scheduled event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings after the close on Tue 2026-10-20 (consensus EPS ~$2.64, revenue ~$2.91B; src 31). Three things make the setup tilt slightly negative versus round 1. (1) Management promised to size Extended Use Instruments 2.0 on this call (src 37); my plausible range is a 1-3% hit to 2027 I&A revenue per procedure, phased in through 2027 (src 37, 38). The Street has not modeled it consistently, so whatever number they give is a headline risk. (2) Q3 2025 procedures grew ~19% (src 45), a tough comp, and the US slowed to 12% in Q2 (src 19, 22); HCA's 10-Q shows exchange admissions -15% and outpatient surgeries -3.4% (src 44). (3) The Fed hiked on 9/16 (src 43) and the 10-year reached ~5.3% on 9/30, highest since 2002 (src 41, 42), which weighs on long-duration growth multiples. The stock also ran ~+15% in September (src 29, 36). On the other side: four straight EPS beats, the EUP is partly priced (HSBC already cut to $391, src 40), short interest is low at 2.31% (src 26), and the EUP number could come in at the benign end (2020 realized ~-2% vs ~-7% modeled, src 39, though that rests on one source). Net: median ~$398.5 (slightly below spot), log sigma ~12% down / ~11% up (37%/3.5 plus an earnings bump, fatter left tail). P(>=401.24)=0.477, a small tilt and not a confident call.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (70%: 2028 EPS $13.25 x 30.5x = $404) and EV/NTM sales (30%: ~$14.4B x 9.0x plus ~$10B cash over ~355M shares = $393) = $401, less a ~$5/share expected-value haircut for the EndoWrist antitrust cases = ~$396. Down from $421 because of the 2027 EUP instrument-price drag and the Fed hike with the 10-year at ~5.0-5.3%.

$11.85 grown ~12%. Elasticity from cheaper instruments supports volume, but the EUP reaches full run-rate and Medicaid work requirements start 1/1/27 (src 28). Tariff exposure stays mitigated by the USMCA exemption (src 2). Was $13.40 in round 1.

bear.story: The Oct 20 EUP sizing lands at the high end (~3% of I&A/procedure, front-loaded). The January 2027 guide is ~10-11% procedure growth as ACA attrition (HCA exchange admissions -15%) is followed by Medicaid work-requirement disenrollment. Ottava and Hugo win price-sensitive accounts, and China tenders keep favoring domestic robots. The 10-year stays above 5% and medtech de-rates further. The hospital class trial (Sep 2027) goes badly. ~$12.0 EPS x ~23x.

base.story: EUP drag of ~2% is phased through 2027 and partly offset by elasticity and Force Feedback. Procedure growth is low-to-mid teens, GM ~68%, and EPS lands slightly below consensus. The multiple drifts to ~30-31x as rates stay high. Litigation is unresolved or settles in the low billions. ~$13.25 2028 EPS x 30.5x.

bull.story: The EUP is sized at the benign end (2020 precedent: ~-2% realized) and elasticity lifts US procedures back toward 15%. dV5 utilization and new indications drive growth, rates ease from 5%+, Ottava and Hugo stay sub-scale, and the class settles cheaply or the en banc petition succeeds. Re-rates to ~39x on ~$13.9.

thesis_break_reason: A close near or below $290 (~28% below today, ~24x 2027 consensus EPS, ~22x my 2028 EPS, well under the $328.57 52-week low) would most likely mean a fundamental break: a 2027 procedure guide near ~10%, an EUP drag well above ~3% of I&A per procedure, visible US share loss or dV5 price cuts against Ottava/Hugo, an adverse hospital-class verdict or injunction that undermines EndoWrist usage-limit economics, or loss of the USMCA exemption. I lowered it from $300, where I depart from the other agents' common level. With the 10-year at ~5.3% and the Fed hiking, a rates-only de-rating to ~25x (~$300) is plausible without anything breaking in the business, so $300 no longer cleanly separates fundamental failure from multiple compression.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's main points against my round-1 file: (a) I never sized the 2027 Extended Use Program 2.0, which management confirmed is 'directionally similar to 2020' and will quantify on the Oct 20 call (src 37); (b) I underweighted rates (Fed hike 9/16, src 43). I ran ~9 follow-ups. They confirmed the EUP is unsized and progressive through 2027 (src 37, 38) and that the 2020 '-7% modeled / -2% realized' benign precedent rests on one Goldman-via-Fool source (src 39), so I use a 1-3% I&A/procedure drag with a 2% midpoint, ~2.5% off EPS. In my lane I found that HSBC had already downgraded to Hold with a $391 target on 7/30 (src 40). I also found that the 10-year closed ~5.29-5.30% on 9/30, highest since 2002 (src 41, 42). That matches agent_5's figure, which the supervisor could not confirm, and is even worse for multiples than the supervisor's ~5.0%. Both sources are secondary (one a search summary), so I treat the level as ~5.0-5.3%. I accept the supervisor's HCA 10-Q figures (src 44) and the ~19% Q3 2025 comp (src 45). Net: 2028 EPS $13.40 -> $13.25, P/E 32x -> 30.5x, EV/sales 9.5x -> 9.0x, fair value $421 -> $396 (supervisor ~$420; I am lower because I put both the EUP and rates fully into the multiple and EPS, and do not assume consensus has absorbed the EUP). I keep the -$5 litigation haircut, as the supervisor endorsed, and add left-tail mass because the class trial is inside the horizon. Scenarios 27% $280 / 50% $405 / 23% $540 (mean ~$402). Ladder: split lognormal, median ~$398, log sigma 36% down / 31% up (around the 37% realized vol); P(>=401)=0.49 (was 0.52), P(>=321)=0.725 (was 0.754). The skeptic findings from round 1 still hold: no short report, short interest 2.31%, small 10b5-1 insider sales, no debt or credit angle. Limits: CNBC and MDDI returned 403, the yield level comes from a search summary plus one brief, and consensus comes from aggregators.
